html:
These views draw the modules the way software draws modules and their interfaces. Each rectangle is a whole module (the SBGN submap glyph, which stands for a pathway drawn elsewhere), and each molecule between two rectangles is an interface: a molecule one module declares as its output and another declares as its input. The arrow runs from the module that makes the molecule; the plain line runs into the module that takes it. One molecule taken by two modules is drawn once, with a line to each.

The particle map and the noise map are two resources (user, 2026-10-30): they share modules, which is the point of cutting maps into modules, but they are planned and assembled apart, so each has its own group of views. These are the particle resource's. A module used by both (the NADPH oxidase, vascular inflammation) is drawn in both, with the same declarations.

Only declared interfaces are drawn: a molecule two modules both draw but do not declare is not a connection here. The views are built from the modules' declarations, so they change when a module's inputs or outputs change.

Open sockets and plugs shows what is missing at the edges of the network. A socket, white on a dashed line entering a module, is an input the module expects from another module of this resource that no module provides. A plug, white on a dashed line leaving a module, is an output no module takes. Inputs from the exposure (the particle, endotoxin, CpG-DNA), cofactors and building blocks (NADPH, oxygen, amino acids, heme) and a module's own proteins are not sockets and are left out.

The planned resource is a proposal: every module the plan names, built ones filled and planned ones white, with the interfaces they would share. An interface not yet declared by both modules is white on dashed lines. Outcomes (COPD, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration) are not modules here, as they belong inside the organ maps. Drawn this way the resource is one network, not separate ones: hydrogen peroxide from the oxidase reaches several modules and nuclear NF-kB four.
